blocks.text: A coconut with a straw in front of a palm-lined beach in San Blas, Panama
San Blas: a coconut drink by the turquoise sea and palm trees

After breakfast, set out on a tour of the historic forts along Panama’s Caribbean coast. Departure is at 08:00. Your first stop is the San Lorenzo Nature Reserve. The Spanish built Fort San Lorenzo in 1596 on a cliff about 25 metres above the sea. From the fort, you can see the Caribbean Sea and the mouth of the Chagres River.

The history of this coast is tied to conquistadors and pirates, including Francis Drake, Henry Morgan and Edward Vernon. King Philip II ordered a network of forts to be built to protect Spain’s possessions. San Lorenzo, San Jerónimo, Santiago de la Gloria, San Fernando and San Fernandín are among the surviving fortifications.

The 17th- and 18th-century colonial buildings and fortifications on Panama’s Caribbean coast were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1980.

The tour continues in Portobelo, where you’ll see the forts and ruins of San Jerónimo, Santiago de la Gloria, San Fernando and San Fernandín, along with the Royal Customs House and the Church of San Felipe, often called the Church of the Black Christ.
